cells.tense: You are reading what is fair inside a situation you cannot see all the way to the end of.
cells.ask: Count three things you gave this month and did not keep score on. Leave the count alone, and let go of one thing you have been holding until it balances.
cells.core:
You can be in the middle of not knowing how this turns out and still feel what is fair. It is a feel, not a calculation — it arrives before you can argue for it, and you have learned to trust the arrival. It also tells you what is owed, including by you, and you act on it without making a display of it.

That steadiness is what keeps the room usable when nobody can see the whole road. The offer part is small: you may put your sense of fairness forward so often that it goes unchallenged from the outside, and the money you are owed sits in someone else's hands while you wait to be fair about it. Say the read out loud some of the time, and let one person decide something on their own, without you smoothing the ground first.

cells.tense: You are auditing fairness against a future that has not arrived yet, and the ledger is running ahead of the events.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are owed and ask for it plainly this week. If no answer comes, leave it open and lend one hand to something that is not yours.
cells.core:
You are checking the fairness of things that have not happened yet. Before anyone has taken anything, you have the split worked out, the odds counted, the compensation priced in — the private scale running on an event that has not landed. Some of that is good sense. Past a point, the foresight stops protecting you and starts holding the situation from resolving, because nothing measures clean until the ending is written in, and you are not there yet.

The bend is what you put into the maybe. A week can go into bracing for a verdict and leave nothing to show. Hand the scale to the situation now and then. Let a problem land on its own before you decide what is fair, and when it lands you will find the verdict mostly written, and it will be lighter than the one you had been drafting ahead of time.

cells.tense: A fairness you would defend stays out of the room now, and the calls come easy without it.
cells.ask: Name one thing that did not sit right lately, out loud, or write it in a line. Then stand by something small nobody is watching, and say out loud that you did it.
cells.core:
There is something fair you would defend if it came up in conversation, and lately it stays out of the room. Decisions get treated as things to get past rather than things to weigh. What is missing is not the sense of right; it is the use of it.

So most calls get made by whatever is easiest, or by whoever speaks first. It can also look like waiting for a setup that is not coming — a version of the situation where an objection would finally land. That version does not arrive on its own. Start smaller. Say the true thing while the subject is still open, and stand by one unremarkable thing that no one would notice if you let it slide. That is the scale coming back into use, and it takes less than the waiting does.

cells.tense: You are already measuring what is fair in ways you would not call fair — the count runs while you call it instinct.
cells.ask: Pick one recent call you made fast and call it a choice. Say why it was right, and set the wondering aside, or settle one of them on the spot.
cells.core:
You have been reading what is fair in rooms nobody asked you to judge. When a meeting goes crooked, you know where it bent. When something is taken from someone, you feel it on your own ledger first and call that instinct, or just how you are. The reading is happening and it is accurate. What is missing is your hand in it.

That is why saying it can feel like accusation: the count has been running with no account for you, so all the wonder also feels like judgment. It is not. It is a sense of what is right, held privately, doing what it does. When it comes up, say the plain thing — this does not seem right, and here is why — and let that be you saying it as yours instead of sounding it out first to see where it stands.
